concurrency.description: Maximum number of queries that are allowed to run concurrently in this reservation. This is a soft limit due to asynchronous nature of the system and various optimizations for small queries. Default value is 0 which means that concurrency will be automatically set based on the reservation size.
concurrency.rationale: Sets the soft limit on concurrent queries in the reservation. This is a capacity/performance-tuning knob teams set for their own workloads; it maps to no security archetype (not exposure, encryption, auth, or destructive-loss), so it is not a platform-level policy target.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

edition.description: The edition type. Valid values are STANDARD, ENTERPRISE, ENTERPRISE_PLUS
edition.rationale: Selects the reservation edition (STANDARD/ENTERPRISE/ENTERPRISE_PLUS). Higher editions gate security-relevant capabilities (e.g. CMEK and stronger governance features), so a whitelist requiring an edition that includes the needed security features fits the secure-tier archetype; the policy should require the tier, not pin one arbitrarily.

ignore_idle_slots.description:
If false, any query using this reservation will use idle slots from other reservations within
the same admin project. If true, a query using this reservation will execute with the slot
capacity specified above at most.
ignore_idle_slots.rationale: Controls whether queries may borrow idle slots from other reservations in the same admin project. This is a capacity-sharing/cost and performance preference within one org's own reservations, not a confidentiality or exposure boundary; it maps to no security archetype and is a team data-management choice.

location.description:
The geographic location where the transfer config should reside.
Examples: US, EU, asia-northeast1. The default value is US.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.description: The name of the reservation. This field must only contain alphanumeric characters or dash.
name.rationale: This is just the reservation name/identifier and does not affect access, permissions, or security settings.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: This only tells Terraform what project to create it in and does not automatically change security settings.

reservation_group.description: The reservation group that this reservation belongs to.

secondary_location.description:
The current location of the reservation's secondary replica. This field is only set for
reservations using the managed disaster recovery feature. Users can set this in create
reservation calls to create a failover reservation or in update reservation calls to convert
a non-failover reservation to a failover reservation(or vice versa).
secondary_location.rationale: This is only used for disaster recovery configuration and does not control access or permissions.

slot_capacity.description:
Minimum slots available to this reservation. A slot is a unit of computational power in BigQuery, and serves as the
unit of parallelism. Queries using this reservation might use more slots during runtime if ignoreIdleSlots is set to false.
slot_capacity.rationale: Defines the minimum slots (compute units) guaranteed to the reservation. This is pure capacity/performance sizing chosen by the team; "must be set correctly to be functional" is a correctness concern, not a security control, and it maps to no archetype.

autoscale.description: The configuration parameters for the auto scaling feature.

autoscale.max_slots.description: Number of slots to be scaled when needed.
autoscale.max_slots.rationale: Sets the autoscale ceiling (slots added on demand). This is a cost/capacity governance knob; cost control and scaling limits are team budgeting decisions, not a security archetype (no exposure, encryption, auth, or data-loss dimension).
